request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 33.9% (95% band 18.4% to 38.7%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.3; 1: +0.6; >= 2: +2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.00, 95% band [+1.66, +2.33]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 17.8% (95% band 10.8% to 23.5%); rank 2 to 3 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 199999: +0.1; >= 200000: -0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.72, 95% band [-1.48, -0.47]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 13.0% (95% band 4.4% to 15.4%); rank 2 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.55 (95% band [-0.88, -0.09]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 18,100 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 4.5% (95% band 0.3% to 7.5%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.17, 95% band [-0.60, +0.46]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 3.4% (95% band 0.4% to 6.4%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.17, 95% band [-0.16, +0.29]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.9% (95% band 0.7% to 10.8%); rank 3 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.37 (95% band [+0.01, +1.21]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 193,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 2.0% (95% band 0.4% to 5.9%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.14, 95% band [-0.03, +0.60]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.0% to 5.4%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.00, 95% band [-0.25, +0.44]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 0.4% (95% band 0.1% to 6.6%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.02, 95% band [-0.28, +0.34]).

Interactions: the model has 22 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 12.2% (95% band 7.3% to 14.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +1.55 (95% band +1.23 to +1.81) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +3.81 (95% band +3.02 to +4.68) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: -0.24 (95% band -0.70 to -0.05) when `PAY_0` = -2, +2.02 (95% band +1.40 to +2.54) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 2.0% (95% band 0.3% to 2.9%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 450,000: -0.71 (95% band -1.55 to -0.45) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -0.77 (95% band -1.48 to -0.41) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,100.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,100: -0.43 (95% band -0.81 to -0.03) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.49 (95% band -0.83 to +0.28) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 450,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & AGE`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.0% to 2.6%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 450,000: -0.60 (95% band -1.26 to -0.36) when `AGE` = 23, -0.77 (95% band -1.63 to -0.46) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.26 (95% band +0.00 to +0.73) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.09 (95% band -0.13 to +0.51) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 450,000.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.0% to 2.1%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 203,000: +0.15 (95% band -0.54 to +0.60) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.22 (95% band -0.60 to +0.48) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,100.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,100: -0.62 (95% band -0.87 to -0.08) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.56 (95% band -1.07 to -0.11) when `BILL_AMT1` = 203,000.
- `PAY_0 & LIMIT_BAL`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.6% to 3.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +1.98 (95% band +1.53 to +2.30) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +2.10 (95% band +1.73 to +2.55) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 450,000.
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 450,000: -0.73 (95% band -1.53 to -0.49) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.61 (95% band -1.40 to -0.27) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_AMT1 & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.0% to 1.8%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,100: -0.43 (95% band -0.84 to +0.08) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.60 (95% band -1.13 to -0.08) when `BILL_AMT2` = 193,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 193,000: +0.41 (95% band +0.02 to +1.26) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.24 (95% band -0.05 to +1.05) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,100.
- 16 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 3.5%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The most important driver of predicted default is repayment status in the latest month (PAY_0): applicants who were paid in full or on time (-1 or 0) are judged much less likely to default, while those with one or more months of payment delay (2 or more) receive a large increase in predicted risk, with a net change of about +2.0 on the log-odds scale between typical low and high values."},{"id":2,"text":"The effect of repayment status is considerably stronger for applicants with a higher education level: moving PAY_0 from -2 to 2 adds about +3.8 log-odds when EDUCATION is 3 (high school), compared with about +1.6 when EDUCATION is 1 (graduate school), so the two features should be read together rather than separately."},{"id":3,"text":"The credit limit (LIMIT_BAL) is the second most important feature: higher limits of 200,000 NT dollars or more are associated with lower predicted default, with a net change of roughly -0.7 log-odds from the low to the high end, and this lower risk holds across the repayment-status levels examined."},{"id":4,"text":"The amount paid in the latest month (PAY_AMT1) is the third most important feature, and larger payments are associated with lower predicted default, with a net decrease of about 0.55 log-odds across its typical range; the shape of this relationship between the endpoints is not resolved by the data."},{"id":5,"text":"The latest bill amount (BILL_AMT1), education on its own, age, and the earlier payment amounts (PAY_AMT2 and PAY_AMT3) show no effect that the data can distinguish from zero, so they should not be treated as reliable drivers of predictions here."},{"id":6,"text":"The bill amount from the previous month (BILL_AMT2) shows a possible increase in risk with higher balances, but its uncertainty band is wide and includes near-zero effects, so the data do not settle whether this effect is real."},{"id":7,"text":"The interaction effects are generally modest in size, and the interactions involving credit limit with payment amount or age, and bill amount with payment amount, have confidence bands that include zero, so the data do not establish them firmly."}]}
